title: Min/Max numeric draft handling is an over-engineered, fully-duplicated 4-field state machine
description: To preserve in-progress numeric text (e.g. "2.0", "-", "0.") while the parent echoes the parsed number back into config, the component maintains a 4-field ScenarioRangeDraftState ({config, committedText, draft, pendingConfigEcho}) per field, a derived selector activeRangeDraft() with 5 branches comparing object identity/committedText/parsed-number equality, plus two near-identical 11-line resync effects (L93-103 and L105-115) carrying eslint-disable for set-state-in-effect, and helper closures setMinDraft/setMaxDraft/updateRangeDraft/commitRangeNumber. The entire apparatus is duplicated verbatim for min and max (every piece of state, every effect, every closure differs only by the Min/Max prefix). This is a lot of bespoke machinery and identity-tracking for a two-field decimal editor. A single small helper hook (e.g. useNumericDraft(committedText, onCommit)) parameterised over the field, or a simpler uncontrolled-with-commit-on-blur pattern, would collapse the min and max copies into one reusable unit and remove the resync effects. NOTE: behavior is currently correct and is pinned by a rich test suite (negative-zero, "0." preservation, cross-node clearing, same-value echo), so any refactor must keep those behaviors; the duplication and identity-comparison complexity are the cleanup target, not a logic change.
evidence: ScenarioRangeDraftState type (L8-13), activeRangeDraft 5-branch selector (L30-46), two duplicated effects (L93-103 / L105-115) each with `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`, and parallel min/max state+closures (L71-91, L127-154). Grep confirms this draft pattern exists in no other editor — it is unique here, not a shared util.
est_reduction: ~40-60 lines (one of the two min/max copies plus one resync effect), depending on extraction approach
behavior_preservation: Must preserve all behaviors encoded in ScenarioExpanderEditor.test.tsx: invalid-draft persistence while editing the same node, '-'/'0.'/'2.0' intermediate text retention, clearing -> onUpdate(null), same-numeric-echo retention, and stale-draft clearing on node switch. Pure structural dedupe/extraction; no semantic change.
